source: Cambodian MAFF/agricultural extension PowerPoint-derived presentation titled "ដំណាំឪឡឹក" (Watermelon), 42 slides; no presenter, publisher, or date named on the slides reviewed. This presentation exists as two near-identical PDF copies in the source set (one with a green-themed slide design, one plain black-on-white reformat of the same 42 slides) - treat as one source, not two corroborating sources.
text:
Watermelon can be planted either by direct seeding into holes in the field, or by raising seedlings in a nursery first and then transplanting.

Direct seeding by hole (ការដាំដោយគ្រាប់ផ្ទាល់): raised beds/ridges are spaced 120-150cm apart (center to center); planting holes are spaced 8-10cm apart along the ridge; row-to-row (clump-to-clump) spacing is about 120cm. A basal mix of manure and compound fertilizer (15-15-15) at about 40kg is applied across 10 planting holes.

Seed preparation for direct seeding: seeds are first sun-dried, then soaked in warm water (about 30-35°C) for 15 minutes; seeds are then washed clean and soaked overnight; seeds are then coated/mixed with Maneb fungicide before planting. Plant 2 seeds per hole; a small amount of Furadan (a carbofuran insecticide) is placed at the bottom of the hole. The hole is then covered with a thin layer of chopped straw/mulch and watered until moist. About 6 days after planting, spray Kinalux 25 (an insecticide) mixed with water in the cool evening.

Nursery method (ការដាំដោយបណ្តុះកូន): seedlings are raised in nursery bags or pots. Use fertile soil mixed with rice husk ash (1 part) and burnt rice husk/charcoal (1 part), totaling about 100kg, mixed with DAP fertilizer (1-1.5kg), compound 15-15-15 fertilizer (2kg), and Furadan 3H insecticide (2 spoons), all mixed thoroughly. Fill the nursery bag or pot to about 2/3 of its height with this mix, then sow the treated seed.

Place 3-4 seeds per bag/pot, cover with soil, then cover with straw mulch for 2 days, watering twice a day. Remove the mulch after 5 days; seedlings can then be transplanted at about that stage.

Spacing note: rows/beds are commonly set about 120cm apart with in-row (clump) spacing also referenced at 120cm, adjusted according to soil type and variety.
